raw_symptom_text: Unusual leaf spot symptoms were observed on rice cultivar Quest; symptoms appeared as diamond-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with grey centres and dark brown margins on leaves and necrotic lesions on panicle neck nodes.
location: Ord River Irrigation Area, Western Australia
citation: You, M.P. et al. (2012). First Report of Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) on Rice (Oryza sativa) in Western Australia. Plant Dis., 96(8), 1224.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms included elliptical, diamond-shaped lesions with gray centers and brown borders on leaf blades and severe neck rot at the base of the panicle causing lodging.
location: Colusa County and Glenn County, California, USA
citation: Greer, C.A. & Webster, R.K. (1997). First Report of Rice Blast Caused by Pyricularia grisea in California. Plant Dis., 81(9), 1094.

raw_symptom_text: Typical blast symptoms were observed on wild rice leaves, presenting eye-shaped and spindle-shaped necrotic lesions with ashen gray centers, rapidly spreading across the field plot under humid conditions.
citation: He, Y. et al. (2022). First Report of Pyricularia oryzae Causing Blast in Wild Rice (Oryza rufipogon) in China. Plant Dis., 106(3), 1063.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms on infected rice plants started as water-soaked stripes along the leaf margins that enlarged into yellow to straw-colored lesions with wavy margins running down the leaf blade, with yellowing leaf tips and uniform wilting of infected tillers.
location: Mwea Irrigation Scheme, Kirinyaga County, Kenya
citation: Nganga, S. et al. (2025). First Report of Bacterial Leaf Blight Disease of Rice Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae in Kenya. Plant Dis., 109(3), 742.

raw_symptom_text: Foliar symptoms on rice cultivar IR841 consisted of elongated water-soaked to yellow lesions with undulating margins along leaf veins, accompanied by rapid yellowing of leaf veins, drying out of leaf tips, and severe blight across the entire canopy.
citation: Afolabi, C.G. et al. (2016). First Report of Bacterial Leaf Blight of Rice Caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae in Benin. Plant Dis., 100(2), 516.

raw_symptom_text: Rice panicles showed conspicuous false smut symptoms where individual grains transformed into yellow-orange velvety smut balls that ruptured and turned dark green to blackened powdery spore masses during late rainy season heading.
citation: Zhou, Y. et al. (2017). First Report of Propiconazole Resistance in Field Isolates of Ustilaginoidea virens on Rice in Jiangsu Province of East China. Plant Dis., 101(6), 1042.

raw_symptom_text: Field symptoms were characterized by transformation of infected rice florets into large rusty-orange to greenish-black smut balls protruding between the glumes, with disease incidence concentrated in the milky ripening stage.
citation: Fang, Y. et al. (2022). Genetic Diversity and Population Structure of the Rice False Smut Pathogen Ustilaginoidea virens in the Sichuan-Chongqing Region. Plant Dis., 106(1), 184-192.

raw_symptom_text: Affected paddy rice plants exhibited severe stunting, leaf chlorosis and yellowing, and when uprooted showed characteristic hooked, swollen root tips with distinct knot-like root galls and root deformation.
citation: Wang, X. et al. (2017). First Report of Meloidogyne graminicola on Rice in Hubei Province of China. Plant Dis., 101(7), 1326.

raw_symptom_text: Rice plants in affected fields were severely stunted with yellowing leaves; root systems displayed characteristic hook-shaped galls at root tips and extensive spindle-shaped root swellings.
citation: Song, Z. et al. (2017). First Report of Meloidogyne graminicola on Rice (Oryza sativa) in Hunan Province, China. Plant Dis., 101(12), 2152.

raw_symptom_text: Larvae bored into rice stem bases, depositing visible frass inside stems, causing dead hearts during the tillering stage and withered whiteheads with empty panicles at heading.
citation: Li, Y. et al. (2025). Advances in the Molecular Mechanisms of Resistance in Chilo suppressalis. Insects, 16(9), 942.

raw_symptom_text: Field infestation of rice plants by yellow stem borer larvae produced bore holes in the stem base with frass, deadheart seedlings where central tillers were easily pulled out, and whitehead symptoms characterized by completely empty upright white panicles.
citation: Sankar, P. et al. (2026). Uncovering resistance traits in rice landraces against Yellow stem borer Scirpophaga incertulas (Walker). Research Square, rs.3.rs-9567632/v1.

raw_symptom_text: Heavy feeding by brown planthopper nymphs and adults at the base of tillers caused rapid plant yellowing, extensive circular patches of dried, lodged plants termed hopperburn, and blackened feeding punctures on lower leaf sheaths.
citation: Zheng, X. et al. (2007). Time of occurrence of hopperburn symptom on rice following root and leaf cutting and fertilizer application with brown planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens. Crop Prot., 26(4), 585-591.

raw_symptom_text: Dense populations of Nilaparvata lugens adults and nymphs aggregated on lower tillers, causing extensive sap depletion, progressive circular hopperburn drying, and prominent blackened feeding puncture scars.
citation: Watanabe, T. et al. (1996). Epiphytic Bacterium, Erwinia ananas, Commonly Isolated from Rice Plants and Brown Planthoppers in Hopperburn Patches. Appl. Entomol. Zool., 31(4), 459-462.

raw_symptom_text: Both adults and nymphs of Leptocorisa oratorius fed on developing rice panicles during milk and dough stages, puncturing individual grains to suck sap, resulting in erect panicles with empty grains, spotted discolored seeds, and rotting panicle tissues emitting a foul odor.
location: Pila and Bay, Laguna Province, Philippines
citation: Jahn, G.C. et al. (2004). Effect of rice bug Leptocorisa oratorius on rice yield, grain quality, and seed viability. J. Econ. Entomol., 97(6), 1923-1927.

raw_symptom_text: Adult insects and nymphs clustered on developing rice panicles, causing severe feeding punctures, diffuse brown necrotic lesions on grains, and empty chaffy grains.
citation: Zhang, H. et al. (2025). Assessing the Population Structure and Invasion Risk in Suitable Areas of the Rice Pest Leptocorisa acuta. Insects, 16(9), 949.

raw_symptom_text: High densities of grasshoppers caused severe defoliation with irregular jagged chewing damage along leaf margins, broad leaf defoliation, and severed maturing panicle stems.
citation: Bao, S. et al. (2019). Cellular response to bacterial infection in the grasshopper Oxya chinensis. Biol. Open, 8(9), bio045864.

raw_symptom_text: Nymph and adult grasshoppers actively consumed rice foliage, exhibiting extensive leaf chewing damage, skeletonized leaves, and cut panicles at the boot stage.
citation: Liu, X. et al. (2026). Transcriptome-wide identification and expression profiling of chemosensory genes in rice grasshopper Oxya intricata. Open Biol., 16(2), 250373.

raw_symptom_text: Infected rice plants showed severe stunting, highly excessive tillering giving a rosette grassy appearance, small rusty necrotic spots on leaves, and complete failure of panicle formation, with brown planthoppers present in the field.
citation: Hibino, H. et al. (1985). Rice Grassy Stunt Virus Strain Causing Tungrolike Symptoms in the Philippines. Plant Dis., 69(6), 538-541.

raw_symptom_text: Field-infected rice plants exhibited pronounced stunting and conspicuous yellow to orange leaf discoloration beginning at leaf tips, accompanied by green leafhopper vectors feeding on foliage.
location: Albay and Camarines Sur, Bicol Region, Philippines
citation: Bajet, N.B. et al. (1986). Occurrence and Spread of Rice Tungro Spherical Virus in the Philippines. Plant Dis., 70(10), 971-973.

raw_symptom_text: Panicle blight symptoms with discolored grains and aborted spikelets were observed on rice; diseased panicles remained upright because of sterile grains, with florets showing brown discoloration on glumes.
citation: Zhou, X. et al. (2020). First Report of Bacterial Panicle Blight of Rice Caused by Burkholderia glumae in Southern China. Plant Dis., 104(4), 1250.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms on rice cultivar Fengliangyou 4 included seedling blight, leaf-sheath browning, bacterial panicle blight, spikelet discoloration, and severe rotting of sterile grains.
citation: Wang, L. et al. (2018). First Report of Burkholderia gladioli Causing Rice Panicle Blight and Grain Discoloration in China. Plant Dis., 102(12), 2634.

raw_symptom_text: Symptoms appeared as oblong pale to dark brown lesions with diffuse margins on the uppermost leaf sheaths enclosing young panicles, with dark brown to grey discoloration of the flag leaf sheath and incomplete panicle emergence with decayed grains.
location: Ord River Irrigation Area, Western Australia
citation: Lanoiselet, V. et al. (2012). First Report of Sarocladium oryzae Causing Sheath Rot on Rice (Oryza sativa) in Western Australia. Plant Dis., 96(8), 1224.

raw_symptom_text: Infected plants displayed prominent longitudinal chlorotic stripes on leaf blades, marked leaf bleaching giving a white leaf appearance, severe plant stunting, and deformed, sterile upright panicles.
citation: Khanal, S. et al. (2025). First Report of Hoja Blanca Viral Disease in Rice in Texas, U.S.A. Plant Dis., 109(5), 1288.

raw_symptom_text: Individual rice grains showed kernel smut symptoms consisting of swollen hulls through which black powdery sooty spore masses of chlamydospores ruptured upon glume opening.
citation: Khanal, S. et al. (2026). First Report and Characterization of Propiconazole Resistance in Tilletia horrida Causing Kernel Smut in Rice. Plant Dis., 110(1), 112-119.

raw_symptom_text: Infected rice plants showed water-soaked streaks that developed into bleached linear stripes on flag leaves, followed by dark brown discoloration of grain hulls and extensive panicle blight.
citation: Xian, P. et al. (2026). First report of rice bacterial blight caused by Pantoea ananatis on rice in Jiangsu Province, China. Plant Dis., 110(2), 488.

raw_symptom_text: Infected rice seedlings displayed abnormal elongation of stems (bakanae symptoms), producing tall, slender, pale yellowish tillers with adventitious root formation at lower nodes and basal foot rot.
citation: Prà, M. et al. (2010). First Report of Fusarium andiyazi Associated with Rice Bakanae in Italy. Plant Dis., 94(8), 1070.

raw_symptom_text: Zinc-deficient rice plants showed distinct brown blotches and bronzing coalescing on the leaf surface 2 to 3 weeks after transplanting, accompanied by interveinal chlorosis, stunted growth, and delayed maturity.
citation: Quijano-Guerta, C. et al. (2002). Tolerance of rice germplasm to zinc deficiency. Field Crops Res., 76(2), 123-130.

raw_symptom_text: Excess ferrous iron in flooded acid sulfate soil caused bronzing of rice leaves, manifesting as numerous tiny brown necrotic spots starting from the tips of older leaves, coalescing into an overall reddish-brown bronzing of the canopy and severe stunting.
citation: Sahrawat, K.L. (2005). Iron toxicity to rice in an acid sulfate soil as influenced by water regimes. Plant Soil, 269(1), 173-178.

raw_symptom_text: Nitrogen-deficient rice leaves exhibited pale yellow-green discoloration, generalized chlorosis across the lower and middle canopy leaves, and reduced tiller numbers.
citation: Kumagai, E. et al. (2009). Effect of nitrogen-deficiency on midday photoinhibition in flag leaves of different rice cultivars. Photosynthetica, 47(2), 241-246.

raw_symptom_text: Under severe drought stress, rice plants exhibited inward leaf rolling of the blade, flaccid leaf wilting, and scorched drying of leaf margins.
citation: Tao, Y. et al. (2024). HD-ZIP IV Gene ROC1 Regulates Leaf Rolling and Drought Response in Rice. Rice, 17(1), 32.

raw_symptom_text: Rainfed lowland rice under terminal vegetative drought experienced severe canopy leaf rolling, accelerated foliar senescence, drying of lower leaf tips, and poor panicle exsertion.
citation: Kumar, A. et al. (2021). Genetic gain for rice yield in rainfed environments in India. Field Crops Res., 260, 107977.

raw_symptom_text: Salt stress in saline paddy soils manifested as white leaf tips, patchy marginal chlorosis, brown scorching of leaf edges, and severely stunted plant development.
citation: van der Ent, A. et al. (2023). Zinc Localization and Speciation in Rice Grain Under Soil Salinity and Deficiency. Plant Soil, 492, 451-464.
